questions.question_text: Determine the parity of (Even * Odd) + Odd.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Even * Odd = Even. Even + Odd = Odd.

questions.question_text: Why is the sum of page numbers on any single loose leaf from a book always odd?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Pages are 2k-1 and 2k. Sum = (2k-1) + 2k = 4k - 1, which is always odd.

questions.question_text: Seven children call out standing height counts: (0, 0, 1, 0, 3, 0, 3). Which child is guaranteed to be the tallest?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The child at position 1 who calls out '0' with nobody ahead is the tallest overall.

questions.question_text: Prove why the center cell 'x' of a 3x3 magic square filled with numbers 1 to 9 must equal 5.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sum of 1..9 = 45. Row sum = 15. Center cell x belongs to 4 lines (row 2, col 2, two diagonals). Adding these 4 lines gives 4*15 = 60. Every cell is counted once, except x which is counted 4 times: 45 + 3x = 60 => 3x = 15 => x = 5.

questions.question_text: Liswini has 50 loose sheets (100 pages printed on both sides). Can the sum of page numbers of all loose sheets be 6000? Explain using parity and sum formulas.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Each loose sheet sum = 4k-1 (odd). Sum of 50 odd numbers is always EVEN. Total sum of first 100 pages = 100*101/2 = 5050. Any 50 sheets from a 100-page book sum to 5050. In a larger book, 50 sheets can sum to 6000 because parity of 50 odd sheets is even and 6000 is even.

questions.question_text: Can 10 odd numbers sum to 100? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Yes. Sum of an even count (10) of odd numbers is always EVEN, and 100 is even.

questions.question_text: Can 9 odd numbers sum to 100? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. Sum of an odd count (9) of odd numbers is always ODD. 100 is even, so impossible.

questions.question_text: In a cryptarithm SEND + MORE = MONEY, determine the single digit values for M and S with logical deduction steps.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Since adding two 4-digit numbers yields a 5-digit number, carry digit M = 1. S + 1 + carry >= 10 => S = 8 or 9. S = 9.

questions.question_text: Construct a 3x3 magic square where numbers used are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. Calculate total sum, row sum, and center cell.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Total sum = 90. Row sum S = 90/3 = 30. Center cell = 30/3 = 10. Magic square elements are 2x standard square [16, 2, 12 / 6, 10, 14 / 8, 18, 4].

questions.question_text: Five children call out (0, 1, 0, 2, 0). Determine who is tallest and who is shortest.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Tallest is child at position 1 (callout 0). Shortest is child at position 4 who has 2 taller ahead.

questions.question_text: Explain the Virahanka-Fibonacci poetic meter rule (short beat S = 1, long beat L = 2) and calculate the number of rhythm combinations for total beat count 6.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Virahanka rule: V(n) = V(n-1) + V(n-2). For beats 1 to 6: V(1)=1, V(2)=2, V(3)=3, V(4)=5, V(5)=8, V(6)=13 combinations.

questions.question_text: A student claims they added 15 odd numbers and got 250. Is this claim mathematically valid? Give full logical proof.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sum of 15 (odd count) odd numbers MUST be an ODD number. 250 is an EVEN number. An odd count of odd numbers can never sum to an even number. The claim is invalid.

questions.question_text: An officer checks logbook entries of 100 pages. 25 loose leaves were removed. Prove whether the sum of page numbers of all removed leaves can equal 2500.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Each loose leaf page sum is odd (4k-1). 25 loose leaves = 25 odd numbers. Sum of 25 (odd count) odd numbers MUST be ODD. 2500 is EVEN. Therefore, the sum of 25 loose leaves can NEVER equal 2500.
